newsitem.title: USA: Gateway up on takeover rumors - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Gateway up on takeover rumors - analysts.

text.p: Gateway 2000 Inc's stock rose Friday on speculation that Compaq Computer Corp had it in its sights as a takeover target, analysts said.
But analysts said that such a possibility was unlikely.
"I don't think it makes sense," said Smith Barney analyst Megan Robertson. "It would have to be a hostile takeover at a premium price, and I don't think Compaq would pay that much."
Gateway's stock ended up 3-3/4 at 59-1/4. A company spokeswoman said Gateway does not comment on rumors. Compaq declined to comment on the rumor.
Oppenheimer & Co's James Poyner discounted the rumor.
"It's a little silly," said Poyner. "If Compaq wanted to be a Gateway, they already have the structure in place. It would be just a matter of marketing."
Smith Barney's Robertson said, "I just don't see it happening."

Earlier, Micron Technology Inc and its 64-percent owned unit Micron Electronics Inc confirmed that they engaged in preliminary discussions with Compaq Computer regarding a potential acquisition by Compaq. However, the companies said in a statement they were not engaged in active discussions and no offer has been received.

Call options in South Dakota-based Gateway, a direct marketer of personal computers, were active as takeover speculation shifted to that company, which was previously rumored to be in talks with Compaq.
But traders said they were skeptical a takeover would occur, noting that the trading pattern was more in keeping with speculators jumping in on rumors.
